ety.text: From Latin fīat (“let it be done”).

senses.d: An arbitrary or authoritative command or order to do something; an effectual decree.
A warrant of a judge for certain processes.
An authority for certain proceedings given by the Lord Chancellor's signature.

ex: All silver content in coins had to be removed from the currency supply, and fiat coins (or tokens) had to take their place.
For quotations using this term, see Citations:fiat.

grp.label: An authoritative command or order to do something; an effectual decree

chain.g: to decide, decide upon, settle, determine (especially something disputed or doubtful)

ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *krey-der. Proto-Italic *krinō Latin cernō Latin dēcernō Latin decretumbor. Portuguese decreto Borrowed from Latin decretum.
